theater: 山東威海衛、馬關與臺灣

battle.name: 乙未戰爭
battle.theater: 山東威海衛、馬關與臺灣
battle.brief: 光緒二十一年，戰火由遼東收束到山東威海衛。日軍以魚雷艇夜襲港內北洋軍艦，再以攻城砲逐座壓制海角砲台，步兵衝鋒入城，北洋水師全軍覆沒；三月日軍渡海入臺，島上以雷管抬槍抵抗至十月。卡面這件雷管步槍，是清軍在威海衛城頭用過的舊式火器，也是日軍十八年式步槍的祖型。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 乙未年即一八九五年，是中日甲午之戰收束的一年，戰場由朝鮮與遼東轉到山東威海衛，並延伸到下關的談判桌與臺灣。日本一方由明治政府主持全局：陸軍方面，攻威海衛的第二軍由陸軍元帥大山岩率領，參謀長樺山資紀參與策劃，另有混成旅團、工兵隊與攻城砲隊配合；海軍方面，一八九四年成立的聯合艦隊由伊東祐亨接掌司令長官，轄裝甲巡洋艦、巡洋艦與魚雷艇隊，其中魚雷艇隊是夜襲威海衛港的主力。臺灣方面設有臺灣總督府，以接收民政事務的名義統合島上軍事部署，作為日軍渡海之前的統帥機關。清方這邊，北洋海軍提督丁汝昌兼領威海衛防衛，地面守備由記名提督馬玉昆等分領各處砲台與城防，守軍總數約四千人上下；北洋艦隊十餘艘退泊港內待修，煤與淡水俱缺，一時不能出港作戰。遼東與山東由北洋陸軍各處駐防，補給線自山東經膠濟、津浦兩線轉往東北，冬季沿途消耗極大。臺灣清軍以唐景崧、劉永福為主，另有丘逢甲等就地組織的義軍。歐洲列強並未參戰，但俄國、法國、德國就遼東問題聯手向日本施壓，英美則居間周旋，維持中立並保全商利。
countriesEn: The year yiwei, 1895, was the year in which the Sino-Japanese War of 1894 was wound up. The battlefield moved away from Korea and Liaodong to Weihaiwei in Shandong, and reached as far as the negotiating table at Shimonoseki and to Taiwan. On the Japanese side the Meiji government directed everything: on land, the Second Army that attacked Weihaiwei was led by the field marshal Oyama Iwao, with the chief of staff Kabayama Sukenori taking part in the planning, and mixed brigades, engineer units and siege artillery cooperating with it; at sea, the Combined Fleet, constituted in 1894 and now under the commander-in-chief Ito Sukeyuki, covered the armoured cruisers, the cruisers and the torpedo-boat squadron, and that torpedo squadron was the instrument of the night attack on the harbour of Weihaiwei. For Taiwan the government set up a governor-general's office which, under the name of taking over the civil administration, unified the military deployment on the island and served as the authority directing the Japanese before they crossed the strait. On the Qing side the admiral of the Beiyang Fleet, Ding Ruchang, held the defence of Weihaiwei together with the land garrison, whose batteries and walls were divided among men such as the titled admiral Ma Yukun, the whole force amounting to some four thousand men; more than ten Beiyang ships lay in the harbour awaiting repair, short of coal and of fresh water, and for the time unable to put to sea. Liaodong and Shandong were garrisoned by units of the Beiyang Army whose line of communication ran from Shandong along the Jiaoji and Jinpu lines towards the north-east, and winter consumption on that route was extreme. The Qing forces in Taiwan were led by Tang Jingsong and Liu Yongfu, and were joined by irregulars raised on the spot by men such as Qiu Fengjia. None of the European powers took part in the fighting, but Russia, France and Germany together pressed Japan on the question of Liaodong, while Britain and the United States kept to the middle, maintaining neutrality and safeguarding their commercial interests without firing a shot.
people: 一八九五年留下姓名的，多集中在三處：清廷的北洋、馬關的談判桌、與臺灣的抵抗。丁汝昌在威海衛陷落前夕服毒自殉，遺書自責未能保船，他留下的絕命詞成為這場戰爭最常被引用的片段；提督劉步蟾在二月十三日夜下令將定遠、鎮遠等殘餘軍艦逐一鑿沉，隨後率殘部向北洋艦隊投降；記名提督馬玉昆分守山東各處，率軍節節退守。臺灣方面，巡撫唐景崧於布袋即位，建立臺灣民主國自任總統，兵敗之後內渡；丘逢甲在臺南以義軍首領身分起兵，失敗後同樣內渡；劉永福守屏東、旗山一線，堅持到十月才由安平登船。日本方面，首相伊藤博文是唯一親赴前線的政治人物，以全權代表身分同李鴻章在馬關往返議約，外務大臣陸奧宗光隨行在側；陸軍元帥大山岩以第二軍司令官身分督率威海衛之役，樺山資紀任參謀長；聯合艦隊司令長官伊東祐亨主持海上的封鎖與夜襲。朝廷內部，翁同龢等主戰派在議和之際被逐出朝廷，李鴻章以簽約之功留任北洋大臣。乙未年五月，康有為、梁啟超聯名上書京師，請求變法。
peopleEn: Those whose names survive from 1895 are gathered in three places: the Beiyang of the Qing court, the negotiating table at Shimonoseki, and the resistance in Taiwan. Ding Ruchang took poison on the eve of the fall of Weihaiwei, leaving behind a letter in which he took the blame for the loss of his ships, and the words he wrote in that last hour are the most frequently quoted fragment of the whole war. The admiral Liu Buchan ordered the remaining Beiyang vessels, the Dingyuan and the Zhenyuan among them, to be scuttled one by one on the night of 13 February, and then led what was left of them into the surrender. The titled admiral Ma Yukun held separate sections in Shandong and withdrew with his men step by step. In Taiwan the governor Tang Jingsong assumed the presidency of the Republic of Formosa at Budai, and left for the mainland after his defeat; Qiu Fengjia rose at Tainan as the head of the righteous armies and likewise crossed to the mainland when they were broken; Liu Yongfu held the line at Pingtung and Qishan until October, when he embarked at Anping. On the Japanese side Prime Minister Ito Hirobumi was the only politician to go near the front, and as the plenipotentiary he negotiated the treaty back and forth with Li Hongzhang at Shimonoseki, with the foreign minister Mutsu Munemitsu at his side. The field marshal Oyama Iwao, commanding the Second Army, directed the operations against Weihaiwei, with Kabayama Sukenori as chief of staff, and the commander-in-chief Ito Sukeyuki conducted the blockade and the night attack at sea. Inside the court, the war party led by Weng Tonghe and the others was pushed out of office at the moment peace was being negotiated, and Li Hongzhang kept his post as North Sea Minister on the strength of having signed the treaty. In the fifth month of the year yiwei, Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao presented a joint memorial to the capital asking for reform.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是法國一八四○年式的雷管步槍：槍尾裝銅製雷管，擊錘敲擊雷管底火引燃火藥，取代了火燧機的燧石打火。好處是霧天、黃昏、雨雪之中都打得響，缺點是槍管與雷管的密閉要求更高，裝藥與壓藥要做得更細緻。日本陸軍走的正是這條路：明治十八年（一八八五）式為前膛雷管步槍，槍身用法國與比利時的米涅式樣本仿製，刺刀另配；明治十三年式原是米涅式前膛槍，後經改良為雷管栓動，兩者同樣以雷管發火，栓動槍只是後起。雷管配上1849年之後推廣的米涅彈，因彈底凹槽受氣膨脹而貼緊膛壁，不必像舊式球彈那樣用布條或油布填膛，射速由每分鐘一兩發提高到十發上下，有效射程可達四百至六百公尺；這正是卡面那句「射程變長，隊形就散了」的來處。清軍這邊，服役最多的仍是前膛雷管抬槍，即一八七二年的古德馬老槍與一八八○年的馬錢壽槍一類，用泥丸加紙包塞膛，射速慢、膛內易留殘渣，遇上潮濕火藥還會啞火。威海衛的守備在海灣砲台與城垣後都用這類抬槍；城破之日，日軍步兵所用的十八年式雷管步槍在巷戰與奪取砲台時成了近戰骨幹。攻城與守城的重火力在日軍是二十四厘米與二十五厘米攻城砲、魚雷艇與加特林機槍；清方是克虜式前膛砲與速射砲，砲台上的加特林多來自進口機與金陵製造局的仿製品。運輸仍靠軍馬、牛車與海運，遼東到山東的補給線在冬季極為艱難。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the French percussion rifle of the 1840 pattern: a copper cap fitted to the breech, which the hammer strikes to ignite the charge, and so it replaces the flint of the musket lock. The advantage is that the weapon fires in fog, at dusk and in rain or snow; the drawback is that the barrel and the cap have to be more tightly sealed, and that the loading and the ramming of the charge have to be done with more care. The Japanese army followed precisely this line: the Meiji year eighteen pattern of 1885 was a muzzle-loading percussion rifle, its stock copied from French and Belgian Minié patterns, with the bayonet issued separately; the Meiji year thirteen pattern was in the first instance a Minié muzzle-loader, later improved into a percussion bolt gun, and both kinds fired by percussion, the bolt action being the newer arrangement. The percussion cap combined with the Minié bullet, introduced after 1849, has a hollowed base that expands with the gases and grips the bore, so that no wad or oiled cloth has to be used to seat the ball as with the old round bullet; the rate of fire rises from one or two rounds a minute to something nearer ten, and the effective range reaches four hundred to six hundred metres. That is where the sentence on the card comes from: the range grew longer, and the formations came apart. On the Qing side the most widely used weapon was still the muzzle-loading percussion tiaiqiang, of the kind represented by the Gud Ma Lao rifle of 1872 and the Ma Qianshou rifle of 1880, which fired clay balls wrapped in paper; these were slow, left fouling in the bore, and if the powder was damp they would misfire. The garrison at Weihaiwei used this sort of rifle behind the batteries of the bay and behind the city walls; on the day the place fell, the Meiji year eighteen percussion rifle in the hands of Japanese infantry became the backbone of the close fighting in the streets and of the storming of the batteries. The heavy weapons of siege and defence on the Japanese side were the twenty-four and twenty-five centimetre siege guns, the torpedo boats and the Gatling guns; on the Chinese side they were Krupp-pattern muzzle-loading guns and quick-firers, and the Gatlings on the batteries came partly from imported machines and partly from the copies turned out at the Jinling Arsenal. Transport still depended on pack horses, ox carts and coastal shipping, and the line of supply from Liaodong to Shandong was bitterly hard in the winter.
tactics: 威海衛一役是海陸並行的攻堅。日軍先以魚雷艇分批夜入港，以艇上雷管魚雷攻擊泊於港內的北洋軍艦，數夜之間擊傷多艘主力艦，港內艦隊自此不能出海；登陸部隊在海灣北岸強行上岸，工兵築壕、架橋、鋪路，把二十四厘米與二十五厘米攻城砲推到砲台射程之內，逐座壓制；步兵在砲火掩護下分隊前進，近到一二百公尺即以刺刀衝鋒，最後攻入城垣，奪取北岸各砲台。守方把海防與陸防分開：北洋艦隊泊在港內，地面部隊分守海角砲台與城垣，兩者之間以書信、旗語與傳令兵聯絡，命令傳遞遲緩，北岸砲台一旦失守，艦隊與城防同時失去依托。清軍在威海衛的砲台是環形配備的固定堡壘，火砲射界良好，但糧食、煤炭與彈藥的補充全靠海運，海路一被封鎖，城內存糧只夠數週。遼東方面，日軍在旅順、大連與營口維持佔領，以鐵路連接山海關與鴨綠江沿岸，用軍馬與牛車輸送，並在沿海修築砲台與塹壕，以防列強干涉。臺灣的戰法與大陸不同：日軍自布袋登陸後，沿縱貫線西段與海岸線北上一路攻取縣城，據點之間以逐次攻取的方式推進；義軍則以游擊與夜襲遲滯日軍，伺其落單時以大刀與獵槍襲擊，因彈藥匱乏、後勤缺乏，戰至年底已難成建制。日軍在臺灣的部隊屢次以縱隊行軍、以白刃解決抵抗，卻在內陸山區屢屢受挫。
tacticsEn: The battle for Weihaiwei was an assault carried out by sea and land together. The Japanese first sent torpedo boats into the harbour by night in successive batches, using the percussion torpedoes carried in the boats to attack the Beiyang ships lying inside, and in the space of a few nights several capital ships were damaged, after which the squadron in the harbour could no longer put to sea. The landing force then went ashore on the north side of the bay, the engineers dug trenches, bridged the streams and laid the roads, and brought the twenty-four and twenty-five centimetre siege guns up inside the range of the batteries, working against them one by one; the infantry advanced in small groups under cover of the gun fire, and at a hundred or two hundred metres went in with the bayonet, and at last entered the walls and carried the batteries on the north shore. The defenders had separated their sea defence from their land defence: the Beiyang squadron lay in the harbour while the ground troops held the coastal batteries and the city, the two linked by letters, flag signals and runners, so that orders travelled slowly, and once the batteries on the north side fell the squadron and the city lost their support together. The Chinese batteries at Weihaiwei were fixed works laid out in a ring, with good arcs of fire, but grain, coal and ammunition were all supplied by sea, and with the sea route closed the stores inside the town could hold out for only a few weeks. In Liaodong the Japanese maintained their occupation of Port Arthur, Talien and Yingkou, linking them by rail to Shanhaiguan and to the coast of the Yalu, moving stores by pack horse and ox cart, and building batteries and entrenchments along the shore in preparation for interference by the powers. The fighting in Taiwan followed a pattern of its own: after landing at Budai the Japanese worked their way up the western section of the trunk line and along the coast, taking the county towns one after another, each strongpoint being reduced in turn; the righteous armies answered with raids and night attacks, falling on the Japanese when they were strayed and cutting at them with heavy blades and hunting guns, and for all their lack of ammunition and of any logistic support they could no longer be organised as a force by the end of the year. The Japanese troops in Taiwan repeatedly marched in column and settled resistance with the bayonet, and were checked again and again in the hills of the interior.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。威海衛之戰自一八九五年一月三十日的海戰起，至二月十七日北洋艦隊投降、日軍入城，再到二月二十一日全區淪陷，合計約三週。海戰中，日軍以聯合艦隊與魚雷艇隊封鎖海灣，港內北洋殘存軍艦約十艘，先後被擊沉或擊傷，另有數艘在投降後移交。陸戰方面，日軍投入第二軍一部與混成旅團，兵力約二萬四千人上下；清方守備連同地面部隊約四千人，陣亡約四千人，日軍陣亡數百至一千餘人，諸說並存。馬關條約於一八九五年四月十七日簽訂，割遼東半島（面積約三萬平方公里）、臺灣全島及澎湖列島，賠款白銀二億兩分十年支付，另有臺灣割讓金三千萬兩，開沙市、重慶、蘇州、杭州為商埠。遼東面積約三萬平方公里，臺灣島面積約三萬五千平方公里，約當九州的三倍。臺灣的戰事自三月底日軍登陸起，到十月全島陷落，前後約七個月，日軍在島上兵力逾三萬，義軍數萬。馬關條約換約在同年六月；同年七月，朝鮮宣佈廢除對清朝的朝貢儀式，名義上脫離宗主關係。步槍本身的數據是：米涅式雷管步槍有效射程四百至六百公尺，全槍重約四公斤，米涅彈每分鐘可發十發上下；抬槍用泥丸，射速每分鐘僅一兩發。加特林機槍每分鐘一百至三百發，射程八百至一千二百公尺，需二至四人操作並另備電源。威海衛方向，日軍二十四厘米與二十五厘米攻城砲各備數門，攻城期間每日發射數百發；日軍在遼東與威海衛的駐軍合計約二萬人上下，直到一八九八年三月遼東交還方才陸續撤走。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The battle for Weihaiwei began with the action at sea on 30 January 1895, passed through the surrender of the Beiyang squadron and the entry of the Japanese into the town on 17 February, and ended with the fall of the whole district on 21 February, about three weeks in all. In the fighting at sea the Japanese Combined Fleet and its torpedo squadron sealed off the bay, the Beiyang squadron in the harbour numbering about ten remaining vessels, which were sunk or damaged in turn, with several more handed over after the surrender. On land the Japanese committed part of the Second Army together with mixed brigades, some twenty-four thousand men or thereabouts; the Chinese garrison and its land force came to about four thousand men, of whom about four thousand were killed, while Japanese dead are put at some hundreds to upwards of a thousand, the estimates varying. The Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed on 17 April 1895, ceding the Liaodong peninsula, of about thirty thousand square kilometres, the whole island of Taiwan with the Pescadores, laying an indemnity of two hundred million taels of silver payable over ten years, with a further thirty million taels for the cession of Taiwan, and opening Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou as treaty ports. Taiwan, of about thirty-five thousand square kilometres, is about three times the size of Kyushu. The fighting in Taiwan ran from the Japanese landing at the end of March to the fall of the island in October, roughly seven months, with over thirty thousand Japanese on the island against tens of thousands of irregulars. The ratifications were exchanged in June of the same year, and in July Korea proclaimed the abolition of the tributary rites towards the Qing court, formally breaking with the suzerain relationship. The figures of the rifle itself are these: the Minié percussion rifle had an effective range of four hundred to six hundred metres and weighed about four kilograms complete, and the Minié bullet could be fired at something near ten rounds a minute, while the tiaiqiang with its clay balls managed one or two rounds a minute. The Gatling fired a hundred to three hundred rounds a minute at a range of eight hundred to twelve hundred metres, needed two to four men to work it and a separate source of power to be carried. At Weihaiwei the Japanese brought up several twenty-four and twenty-five centimetre siege guns, firing several hundred shells a day during the siege; the Japanese garrisons in Liaodong and at Weihaiwei together came to about twenty thousand men, and were not withdrawn until the territory was handed over in March 1898.
cause: 把戰火拖到一八九五年的原因，一半在戰局，一半在外交。軍事上，旅順、大連與黃海的制海權在甲午年已經易手，北洋五艘主力艦在黃海海戰失去戰鬥力，清廷在朝鮮與遼東的地面部隊又屢戰屢退；到了年末，能與日本抗衡的只剩下威海衛一處海灣與泊在港內的北洋殘艦，而補給、燃煤與糧食全靠海運，海路一封，這支艦隊就只是一批待修的鋼鐵。威海衛若失守，京畿的門戶洞開，清廷也再無談判籌碼，議和遂成唯一選項。外交上，日本在朝鮮與遼東的既得既深，願意停手，但要求割地與賠款；俄國自一八九一年取得旅順租借地之後，希望限制日本在滿洲的勢力，於是與法國、德國聯手向日本施壓，三國干涉的種子正是在一八九五年春天播下的。臺灣方面，清廷接到日本割臺要求後拖延交割，島上官紳自行組織義軍以拒日，又援引條約反對日本渡海，此舉反而給了日本用兵的口實。朝廷內部，主戰與主和之爭在乙未年達到頂點，翁同龢等主戰派被逐出朝廷，北洋系的李鴻章接手議和。
causeEn: What carried the fighting on into 1895 was half a matter of the military situation and half a matter of diplomacy. On the military side Port Arthur, Talien and command of the Yellow Sea had already changed hands in the year of jiawu; the five Beiyang capital ships had been knocked out of the fight in the Battle of the Yellow Sea; and the Qing ground forces in Korea and Liaodong had been beaten back again and again. By the end of the year the only thing left that could hold Japan at bay was the single bay of Weihaiwei and the remnant of the Beiyang squadron lying in its harbour, and that squadron's supply, coal and food all came by sea, so once the sea route was shut it was nothing but a batch of steel waiting to be repaired. If Weihaiwei fell, the gates of the capital district stood open, and the Qing court would have no card left to play: negotiation was the only course left. In diplomacy, Japan's existing gains in Korea and Liaodong were deep, and it was willing to stop fighting but asked for territory and money. Russia, which had held the lease of Port Arthur since 1891, wanted to limit Japan's position in Manchuria, and so joined with France and Germany in pressing Japan; the seed of the tripartite intervention was sown in the spring of 1895. In Taiwan the Qing court, having received the Japanese demand for cession, put off the handover, the gentry and officials of the island raised irregulars of their own to resist, and invoked the treaty against any Japanese crossing of the strait; that very step gave Japan the pretext to use force. Inside the court the quarrel between the war party and the peace party reached its height in the year yiwei, the war party led by Weng Tonghe was driven out of office, and the Beiyang group under Li Hongzhang took over the negotiation.
impact: 這場戰爭的餘波遠比戰場本身長。割地賠款之後，清廷的財政被壓到懸崖：二億兩白銀分十年支付，須靠對外借款與加派才能湊齊，沿海各省的稅源被抵押，財政與主權一齊流失。遼東半島先割予日本，一八九五年四月至十一月俄法德三國聯名交涉，十一月日本答應歸還，一八九六年商定界址，一八九八年三月正式交付；這是近代中國第一次靠自己的外交收回失地，卻也是列強在遠東聯手行動的開端。此後德國於一八九五年十一月藉口山東教案出兵占領膠州灣，英國在一八九八年租借威海衛，俄國取得旅順與大連的租借地，沿海各省一一被列強環伺。國內方面，北洋水師覆沒刺激起重建之論，一八九八年清廷設海軍衙門，江南、福州、天津各機器局相繼開爐造艦，試圖在十年間重建海軍；湖北槍炮廠同時擴產，栓動步槍自此成為主流，卡面上的雷管前膛槍在軍械庫中慢慢退到次要位置。學術與思想方面，康有為、梁啟超在乙未年五月的公車上書要求變法，甲午的敗績成了維新最有力的理由；台灣割讓之後島上另建臺灣民主國，義軍以雷管抬槍與大刀抵抗日軍到十月才逐漸平息，往後五十年是日本殖民統治的開端。朝鮮在條約中失去宗主地位，俄系外交官一度在漢城得勢，翌年王室事件更引出英俄在遠東的角力。日本則以這場勝利為起點，確立向大陸推進的國策，戰後擴軍計劃把軍費推上高峰，十年後的日俄戰爭已在此時埋下伏線。
impactEn: The aftershocks of this war ran a great deal further than the battlefield itself. After the cession and the indemnity the Qing treasury was pressed to the edge of a cliff: two hundred million taels of silver payable over ten years could only be raised by foreign loans and additional levies, the revenue of the coastal provinces was pledged, and treasury and sovereignty drained away together. The Liaodong peninsula was ceded to Japan first; from April to November 1895 Russia, France and Germany pressed the point jointly, Japan agreed in November to give it back, the boundary was fixed in 1896, and the territory was formally handed over in March 1898. That was the first time in modern history that China recovered lost territory by its own diplomacy, and equally the opening of joint action by the powers in the Far East. Afterwards Germany occupied the bay of Kiaochow in November 1895 on the pretext of a religious incident in Shandong, Britain leased Weihaiwei in 1898, Russia obtained the leases of Port Arthur and Talien, and the coastal provinces were ringed one after another by the powers. At home, the loss of the Beiyang Fleet stirred up the argument for rebuilding it: the court set up a naval administration in 1898, and the arsenals at Nanking, Fuchow and Tientsin were successively lit to build warships, in the hope of recreating a navy within ten years. The Hubei Gun Foundry expanded production at the same time, the bolt-action rifle became the standard, and the percussion muzzle-loader on the card quietly fell back to a secondary place in the arsenals. In thought and letters, the memorial which Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao presented in the fifth month of the year yiwei asked for reform, and the defeat of the war of 1894 became the strongest argument for the reformers. After Taiwan was ceded, the island raised the Republic of Formosa, and the righteous armies fought the Japanese with percussion tiaiqiang and heavy blades until the resistance died out in October, heralding fifty years of Japanese colonial rule. Korea lost its suzerainty under the treaty, Russian-oriented officials were for a time in the ascendant at Seoul, and the incidents surrounding the royal household the following year drew in the rivalry of Britain and Russia in the Far East. For Japan the victory was the starting point of a continental policy: the post-war expansion plan pushed military spending to a new peak, and the Russo-Japanese War of ten years later was already prepared for in all this.
result: 結果是北洋艦隊覆沒、威海衛陷落、清廷割地賠款。一八九五年一月三十日至二月二日，日軍以魚雷艇與聯合艦隊封鎖威海衛，港內北洋軍艦相繼被擊傷或自沉；二月十三日夜劉步蟾下令鑿沉定遠、鎮遠等殘餘軍艦，二月十六日丁汝昌服毒自殉，二月十七日北洋艦隊投降、日軍入威海衛城，二月二十一日全區淪陷，日本自此控制渤海灣，京畿與直隸的門戶洞開。四月十七日李鴻章與伊藤博文在馬關赤間關港簽訂條約，割遼東半島與臺灣、澎湖，賠款二億兩，開四處商埠，六月換約。十一月俄法德三國干涉，日本答應歸還遼東，三年後交付。臺灣方面，日軍於三月底自布袋登陸，五月二十三日唐景崧在布袋即位為臺灣民主國總統，六月臺南府城失守，澎湖諸島亦相繼為日軍所占，義軍在劉永福、丘逢甲等人率領下節節抵抗，到十月全島淪陷、劉永福內渡，戰事至此收束，島上進入五十年日治時期。清朝在甲午、乙未兩役之後元氣盡失：北洋水師一去不返，淮軍體系瓦解，國內反清的暗流與維新思潮同時升溫。日本則以這場勝利確立向大陸推進的國策，十年後的日俄戰爭已在此時埋下伏線。
resultEn: The result was the destruction of the Beiyang Fleet, the fall of Weihaiwei, and cession and indemnity by the Qing court. From 30 January to 2 February 1895 the Japanese sealed off Weihaiwei with their torpedo boats and the Combined Fleet, and the Beiyang ships in the harbour were damaged or scuttled one after another. On the night of 13 February Liu Buchan ordered the remaining vessels, the Dingyuan and the Zhenyuan, to be sunk; on 16 February Ding Ruchang took poison; on 17 February the Beiyang squadron surrendered and the Japanese entered the town of Weihaiwei; and on 21 February the whole district fell, leaving Japan in control of the Gulf of Bohai and the gates of the capital district and of Zhili open. On 17 April Li Hongzhang and Ito Hirobumi signed the treaty at the port of Akama near Shimonoseki in Yamaguchi, ceding the Liaodong peninsula with Taiwan and the Pescadores, imposing two hundred million taels of indemnity and opening four treaty ports, the ratifications being exchanged in June. In November Russia, France and Germany intervened, Japan agreed to return Liaodong, and the handover took place three years later. In Taiwan the Japanese landed at Budai at the end of March; on 23 May Tang Jingsong assumed the presidency of the Republic of Formosa at Budai; in June Tainan fell, and the Pescadores were taken by the Japanese in turn; the righteous armies under men such as Liu Yongfu and Qiu Fengjia resisted step by step until the island fell in October and Liu Yongfu crossed to the mainland, which ended the fighting and began fifty years of Japanese rule on the island. After the wars of jiawu and yiwei the Qing dynasty was spent: the Beiyang Fleet was never restored, the Huai Army system fell apart, and the undercurrents of opposition to the Qing and the current of reform both rose at the same time. Japan, for its part, fixed upon a continental policy on the strength of this victory, and the Russo-Japanese War of ten years later had been prepared for in all that.
